A 64 MiB BF16 all-reduce is 67.1 MB. NVLS offloads the reduction to the NVSwitch, so each GPU sends the data once and receives the reduced result once. Per-GPU traffic is therefore about 1× the message size, compared with about 2× for a ring.

NVLink 5 gives roughly 900 GB/s per direction per GPU. NCCL NVLS typically reaches about 55–60% of that at large sizes, so algorithmic bandwidth is about 500 GB/s. At 64 MiB the pipeline is not fully saturated, so I assume about 400 GB/s effective, which gives about 168 µs. Adding about 20–30 µs for launch, switch and pipeline-fill latency across 72 GPUs brings the total to about 190 µs.

This is an estimate from typical NVLS efficiency, not a measurement.
